practices.practice: Read DOCUMENTDB_URI from an environment variable and create a single shared MongoClient at process startup, reusing that client across modules instead of opening a new connection per request.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI from an environment variable (not checked into source) and create a single shared MongoClient at app startup; reuse that client across modules instead of opening a new connection per request.

practices.practice: Tune MongoClient pool and timeout settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) based on your environment (serverless vs long-running) and expected concurrency.
practices.prior_belief: Tune MongoClient pool settings in the connection string (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) and enable unified topology; set reasonable serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS so the app detects and recovers from unreachable cluster quickly.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Always require TLS/SSL (e.g., tls=true/ssl=true in the connection string) and do not disable certificate validation when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: Do not commit database credentials or connection strings to source control; load secrets from environment variables or a secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) and follow least-privilege access for retrieval.
practices.prior_belief: Do not store database credentials or connection strings in the repository; load secrets from environment variables or a secrets store (Azure Key Vault) and grant the app least-privilege access to them.
practices.source_name: How to choose between standard (manual) and autoscale provisioned throughput

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC or otherwise use a dedicated least-privilege account for application access rather than a cluster admin credential.
practices.prior_belief: Use a dedicated, least-privilege database user for the application (not the cluster admin), with only the minimum roles/privileges needed to read/write the application collections.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and rate-limit responses (handle 429/Retry-After), and enable the driver's retryReads/retryWrites where appropriate.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and rate-limited responses (handle HTTP 429/Retry-After from Cosmos), and enable retryableWrites where appropriate.

practices.practice: Perform slot booking with an atomic conditional update (e.g., findOneAndUpdate or updateOne with filter { _id: slotId, status: 'available' } and check the returned/modified count) to detect conflicts instead of a separate read-then-write.
practices.prior_belief: Perform slot booking/rescheduling with an atomic conditional update (e.g., updateOne({_id:slotId, status:'available'}, {$set:{status:'booked', appointmentId:...}})) and check modifiedCount to detect conflicts instead of separate read-then-write.

practices.practice: Use multi-document transactions (session.withTransaction) when supported by the cluster's MongoDB API version to make related updates atomic; if transactions are unavailable, use a compensated pattern and detect partial failures.
practices.prior_belief: For multi-document invariants (e.g., create appointment document AND mark slot booked), use a multi-document transaction when supported by the MongoDB API version in the cluster; otherwise implement a safe compensating pattern and detect partial failures.

practices.practice: Create a compound index that matches common availability queries (example: { providerId: 1, start: 1, status: 1 }) and make index creation idempotent in seed scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index supporting the most common availability queries, for example {providerId:1, startTime:1, status:1}, and ensure index creation is idempotent in the seed script.

practices.practice: Enforce uniqueness at the database level by creating unique indexes for fields that must be unique (e.g., appointment reference or other application-unique keys) instead of relying only on application checks.
practices.prior_belief: Use unique indexes for fields that must be unique (e.g., appointment._id or a unique appointmentReference) and enforce uniqueness at the DB level where possible; do not rely solely on application checks to prevent duplicates.

practices.practice: When storing embeddings for vector search, store them as consistent-dimension numeric arrays and create a vector index with the correct dimension and similarity metric (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) supported by the cluster.
practices.prior_belief: If storing embeddings for vector search, store them as a consistent-dimension numeric array (e.g., embedding: [float,...]) and create a vector index configured with the correct dimension and metric (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) supported by the cluster.

practices.practice: Provision throughput sensibly: use autoscale or an appropriately sized provisioned throughput at the collection or database level for your workload, and prefer collection-level throughput for predictable isolation.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput sensibly: use autoscale or an appropriately sized RU/s for the database/collection; for development use lower single-collection throughput and for production scale based on load and RU cost of booking flows.
practices.source_name: Provision database, container or autoscale throughput on Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB resources

practices.practice: Monitor RU consumption and throttle/back off on 429 responses; use Azure Monitor / diagnostic settings to observe RU usage and autoscale behavior.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU consumption and avoid operations that require large RU spikes (large scans, unindexed sorts); respond to 429 by backing off and throttling client request rate.
practices.source_name: How to choose between standard (manual) and autoscale provisioned throughput

practices.practice: Avoid unbounded collection scans: always filter on indexed fields and use projection to return only necessary fields to reduce RU cost and latency.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid unbounded collection scans: always filter on indexed fields and use projection to only return required fields (e.g., when listing availability return providerId, startTime, duration, status only).

practices.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent: create collections and indexes only if they don't exist and use upsert/guards so running seed multiple times does not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Make the seed script idempotent: create collections and indexes only if they don't exist, and use upsert operations or checks so running seed multiple times does not create duplicates.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral records by indexing a Date field (expireAt/createdAt) with expireAfterSeconds; remember the field must be a Date and expiry is not second-accurate.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral records (e.g., temporary holds or short-lived conversation state) by adding an ISODate field (expireAt) and a TTL index so the DB automatically expires stale data.

practices.practice: Prefer findOneAndUpdate (or similar find+modify) with an appropriate returnDocument option to update documents in-place atomically and return the final state for use in application state/memory.
practices.prior_belief: When updating documents in place prefer findOneAndUpdate with an atomic modifier and an appropriate returnDocument option (return the new state) to reduce round-trips and ensure you get the final state to update memory/agent context.

practices.practice: Avoid storing or logging sensitive patient information in plaintext; redact or omit PII from logs and use encryption for backups and at-rest storage (CMK) where required by compliance.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing or logging sensitive patient information in plaintext in logs; redact or omit PII from logs and secure exported DB backups.

practices.practice: Persist only minimal identifiers for agent conversational memory (conversationId, lastAppointmentId) and keep full conversational context ephemeral; encrypt persisted sensitive state at rest when required.
practices.prior_belief: For conversation memory and agent state, persist only necessary identifiers (conversationId, lastAppointmentId) in the DB and keep full conversational context ephemeral in the agent memory; encrypt sensitive persisted state at rest if required.
practices.how_found: azure documentdb conversation memory persistence; azure documentdb pii logs memory storage; documentdb encryption conversation state

practices.practice: For free-text search prefer the platform text/search features (DocumentDB's textSearch / $search) and scope text indexes to only the fields required to limit index size and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Create text indexes for free-text search fields (e.g., provider name, specialty) if the app needs text search, and restrict text indexes to the fields actually needed to limit index size and RU cost.

practices.practice: Model for access patterns: keep one slot document per slot and a separate appointments collection that references slotId so you can target atomic updates on slots without large document rewrites.
practices.prior_belief: Design documents for the access patterns: keep a single slot per document (slot document) and a separate appointments collection that references slotId, to allow targeted atomic updates on slots without large document rewrites.

practices.practice: Protect the DocumentDB cluster with network restrictions (IP firewall rules or Private Endpoint / VNet) to limit access to authorized hosts only.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the Cosmos account with network restrictions (IP firewall rules or VNet/private endpoint) so only allowed application hosts can reach the DocumentDB endpoint.

practices.practice: When rescheduling slot times, check for overlapping slots for the same provider using indexed queries and enforce application-level checks to prevent overlapping bookings because DB-level partial unique constraints on time ranges are not a general replacement.
practices.prior_belief: When performing reschedule logic that changes slot times, check for overlapping slots for the same provider using an indexed query and enforce application-level checks to prevent overlapping bookings (DB-level partial unique constraints on time ranges are not broadly supported).
practices.how_found: azure documentdb overlapping time ranges unique constraint; mongodb partial unique index time ranges; documentdb enforce non-overlapping time ranges

practices.practice: Instrument and trace booking and rescheduling flows (record latency, RU cost, success/failure) and surface slow queries and RU hotspots through diagnostic settings and Log Analytics alerts.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and trace booking/rescheduling flows (record latency, RU cost, success/failure) so you can detect hotspots and tune indexes or RU provisioning accordingly.

practices.practice: Include fields used for sorting (e.g., start) in your index prefix so queries that sort can avoid an in-memory blocking SORT; follow the ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) rule when designing compound indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Index the fields used for sorting (e.g., startTime) so that queries that sort by startTime can use an index rather than a blocking sort; prefer covered queries (projection includes only indexed fields) where possible to reduce RU.
